articles.title: T.N. govt. to establish five Model Registration Hubs in first phase
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens will be able to register property documents and marriages at any hub of their choice, irrespective of the jurisdiction of Sub-Registrar Office; govt. to expand initiative to more locations

The Tamil Nadu government has accorded sanction for setting up Model Registration Hubs (MRH) at five locations across the State in the first phase at a cost of ₹7.84 crore on a pilot basis, with plans to expand the initiative to 20 more locations in subsequent phases.

A Government Order to this effect has been issued by the Commercial Taxes and Registration Department. The MRH will be established in the Chennai North, Chennai Central, Chennai South, Chengalpattu and Coimbatore registration districts in the first phase.

The MRH concept expands the single-window, jurisdiction-free registration facility, enabling citizens to register documents and marriages at any MRH of their choice, irrespective of the territorial jurisdiction of the Sub-Registrar Office concerned over the property or the parties involved, the order said.

The MRH have been classified into three categories based on the volume of document and marriage registrations, while retaining uniform service standards and a consistent citizen experience. The Category I MRH will have an area of 8,000 sq. ft., seating capacity for 100 people with 20 workstations. The Category II MRH will have 5,000 sq. ft., with seating for 75 people with 15 workstations, while the Category III MRH will have an area of 3,000 sq. ft., seating for 50 people with 10 workstations. All three categories will be equipped with the necessary IT and non-IT equipment.

The capital expenditure and operational responsibilities for establishing and running the MRH will be entrusted to a Managed Service Provider (MSP) selected through a competitive tendering process. However, all statutory registration processes will remain with the Sub-Registrar concerned. The order also noted no additional posts would be created for establishing these MRHs and District Registrars and Sub-Registrars would be redeployed to staff these facilities.

The MRH will offer two types of services such as standard and premium. articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 30 Oct 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 T.N. govt. to establish five Model Registration Hubs in first phase

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Citizens will be able to register property documents and marriages at any hub of their choice, irrespective of the jurisdiction of Sub-Registrar Office; govt. to expand initiative to more locations

The Tamil Nadu government has accorded sanction for setting up Model Registration Hubs (MRH) at five locations across the State in the first phase at a cost of ₹7.84 crore on a pilot basis, with plans to expand the initiative to 20 more locations in subsequent phases.

A Government Order to this effect has been issued by the Commercial Taxes and Registration Department. The MRH will be established in the Chennai North, Chennai Central, Chennai South, Chengalpattu and Coimbatore registration districts in the first phase.

The MRH concept expands the single-window, jurisdiction-free registration facility, enabling citizens to register documents and marriages at any MRH of their choice, irrespective of the territorial jurisdiction of the Sub-Registrar Office concerned over the property or the parties involved, the order said.

The MRH have been classified into three categories based on the volume of document and marriage registrations, while retaining uniform service standards and a consistent citizen experience. The Category I MRH will have an area of 8,000 sq. ft., seating capacity for 100 people with 20 workstations. The Category II MRH will have 5,000 sq. ft., with seating for 75 people with 15 workstations, while the Category III MRH will have an area of 3,000 sq. ft., seating for 50 people with 10 workstations. All three categories will be equipped with the necessary IT and non-IT equipment.

The capital expenditure and operational responsibilities for establishing and running the MRH will be entrusted to a Managed Service Provider (MSP) selected through a competitive tendering process. However, all statutory registration processes will remain with the Sub-Registrar concerned. The order also noted no additional posts would be created for establishing these MRHs and District Registrars and Sub-Registrars would be redeployed to staff these facilities.

The MRH will offer two types of services such as standard and premium. The fee for standard document and marriage registration services has been fixed at ₹2,000, while the fee for tatkal standard services will be ₹5,000. The revenue will be shared between the Registration Department and the service provider in an 80:20 ratio.

The fee for premium document and marriage registration services has been fixed at ₹5,000, with the revenue shared equally between the department and the service provider, while the fee for tatkal premium services will be ₹10,000, with the revenue shared in a 65:35 ratio, the order added.

articles.title: Ex-Mayor Bhagyalakshmi appeals to voters to give her another opportunity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Mayoral candidate Rayana Bhagyalakshmi on Thursday appealed to voters to give her another opportunity to serve as Mayor, adding that the city had witnessed significant development during the party’s previous five-year tenure.

Addressing the media in Gandhi Nagar, Ms. Bhagyalakshmi said the party was committed to accelerating urban development and remaining accessible to the public. She urged voters to elect her and the party’s corporator candidates in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections.

Alleging that the coalition government had failed to deliver on its promises, she questioned the development works undertaken in Vijayawada over the past three years. She claimed that the previous YSRCP government had improved water tanks, drainage systems, parks, community halls and the Ajit Singh Nagar dumping yard. She also cited the construction of a retaining wall in Krishnalanka as a major achievement.

YSRCP NTR district president Devineni Avinash said Ms. Bhagyalakshmi had discharged her responsibilities as Mayor with commitment and helped the city secure awards during her tenure. He appealed to voters to support all 86 YSRCP corporator candidates.

Former Minister Vellampalli Srinivasa Rao alleged that the coalition government had failed to take adequate measures to address Vijayawada’s civic problems, including flooding and drainage issues. He claimed that the previous YSRCP government had undertaken significant development works and expressed confidence that his party would win the municipal elections.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

In a visit to fine-tune the details of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah ’s planned trip to India, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is expected to reach Kathmandu on November 4, along with newly designated Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela, a Nepali diplomatic source has told The Hindu .

Mr. Shah is expected to visit India by the end of the year, even as his seven-month-old government continues to deal with the aftermath of the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River while also planning a slew of administrative and political reforms.

If it materialises, this will be the first bilateral visit abroad by Mr. Shah, who rose to prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising in Nepal that overthrew the government of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Shah, who belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) led by former media personality Rabi Lamichhane, had vowed to focus on domestic priorities while deprioritising foreign interlocutors. In fact, Mr. Misri was earlier scheduled to travel to Kathmandu to meet Prime Minister Shah in May but the visit was postponed, ostensibly because of the new leader’s resolve to focus on domestic challenges.

Subsequently, RSP chairman Mr. Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 3, after which Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal visited Delhi on June 5, in the first Minister-level representation to India from the new government, and met his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. This was followed by the visits of Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in September and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who participated in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) Home Ministers’ meeting held on October 13. Mr. Gurung also met Mr. Jaishankar before he returned to Kathmandu. Mr. Wagle paid a repeat visit to New Delhi to participate in a private media conclave on October 23, when he also had a courtesy meeting with the Prime Minister.

Despite the flurry of visits, the Embassy of Nepal here has been left without an Ambassador for some months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Diplomatic sources said that the appointment of a new Nepali Ambassador to India will feature in the talks with Mr. Misri.

Nepal now has a complex new process to appoint envoys, as the new government announced that top ambassadorial posts would be selected through a public application process. In all, around 4,400 candidates had applied for the vacant ambassadorial positions. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu that Kathmandu is awaiting the agrément (diplomatic permission) from India for Nischal Nath Pandey’s arrival in the Nepali Embassy in Delhi. Of the top ambassadorial posts in 13 Nepali missions, three remain uncertain, while Mr. Pandey’s name, along with nine others, has received the necessary clearance in Kathmandu.

Mr. Misri’s upcoming visit is also expected to review Nepal’s requirements for dealing with the aftermath of the disaster in the Bhote Koshi River, which affected hundreds of Indian families as well, as many individuals remain missing.

The Foreign Secretary is likely to meet Mr. Lamichhane, who earlier this week paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. The RSP chairman, who travelled to Uttarakhand by road from western Nepal, had described his visit to these pilgrimage centres as “personal and not political”.

“There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” he said, before starting his pilgrimage in his second visit to India in six months.

articles.title: Kauvery Hospital treats complex aortic valve disease using HANCHOR technology
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Aortic regurgitation is a condition in which the heart’s aortic valve fails to close properly, causing blood to flow backwards into the heart

Kauvery Hospital, Alwarpet, Chennai, has treated a 63-year-old man with severe leakage in his aortic valve using a minimally invasive procedure called transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), the hospital said at a press conference. The patient had a hole in one of the leaflets of his aortic valve and had previously undergone mitral valve replacement.

Aortic regurgitation occurs when the aortic valve does not close properly, allowing blood to flow backwards into the heart. Treating this condition through a catheter-based procedure can be challenging because the valve may not have enough calcium deposits to help secure the replacement valve. The patient’s previous mitral valve replacement added to the complexity.

The HANCHOR valve has a frame that expands with a balloon and a special anchoring mechanism made of nitinol, a flexible metal alloy. This mechanism is designed to hold the replacement valve securely in place by gripping the existing valve leaflets.

The hospital said checks after the procedure showed no remaining leakage through or around the replacement valve and no abnormal narrowing. No significant problems with the heart’s electrical signals were reported. The patient was discharged three days later.
Rajaram Anantharaman, senior consultant interventional cardiologist said the valve’s anchoring mechanism helped address the challenges of positioning the replacement valve in this case.
Asik Ali, senior consultant and clinical lead, Cardiac Imaging Radiology; Mahesh Kumar K., medical superintendent; and Kamal Kanth, consultant cardiologist, were also present at the press conference.

• Aortic regurgitation is a condition in which the heart’s aortic valve fails to close properly, causing blood to flow backwards into the heart
• Kauvery Hospital, Alwarpet, Chennai, has treated a 63-year-old man with severe leakage in his aortic valve using a minimally invasive procedure called transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), the hospital said at a press conference. The patient had a hole in one of the leaflets of his aortic valve and had previously undergone mitral valve replacement.
• Aortic regurgitation occurs when the aortic valve does not close properly, allowing blood to flow backwards into the heart. Treating this condition through a catheter-based procedure can be challenging because the valve may not have enough calcium deposits to help secure the replacement valve. The patient’s previous mitral valve replacement added to the complexity.

articles.title: Jailhouse rock, the ‘others’ in the dock
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A doctor serving Odisha’s tribal heartland was arrested for allegedly supporting the resistance against bauxite mining. His name, along with those of other activists, did not figure in the FIR, but the police arrested them under a category of unnamed ‘others’. Satyasundar Barik speaks to Adivasi and Dalit communities, which allege the police are using the legal process for intimidation

It was close to 11 p.m. on October 16. A posse of police personnel knocked on the door of a rented house in Hilltown, Bhawanipatna, the headquarters of Odisha’s Kalahandi district. Dr. Randall Sequeira, 39, opened the door. He was arrested along with Laxman Naik, a 31-year-old Dalit activist who was also in the house.

The following day, the police linked their arrests to a violent clash that had taken place 192 days earlier. Neither Sequeira nor Naik were among the 26 villagers initially named in FIR No. 85/2026, which was registered at the Kashipur police station in the neighbouring Rayagada district. Instead, the police added them later. They were allegedly identified from a category of 100 unnamed ‘others’ from Kantamal town, in Rayagada’s Kashipur, mentioned in the FIR.
Political & National Report: Jailhouse rock, the ‘others’ in the dock. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Police barged into my office to arrest former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, alleges senior advocate P. Wilson in Madras HC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: However, State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan denies the allegation and says the police were actually invited into the office but they did not arrest the accused inside the lawyer’s office

Senior counsel P. Wilson on Thursday (October 29, 2026) complained to the Madras High Court that Central Crime Branch (CCB) police personnel “barged” into his office in Chennai on October 26, 2026 to arrest former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi (DMK) in a case booked on charges of allegedly collecting over ₹400 crore towards ‘party fund’ from more than 177 private school managements in the State.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, seized of a plea by the former Minister to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against him, the senior counsel said, the petitioner was at his office on Nelson Manickam Road at about 3 p.m. on Monday to discuss about the further course of legal action to be taken pursuant to the dismissal of his anticipatory bail petition by the High Court.

“We were discussing at our office regarding further course of legal action. About three vans of 40 policemen came to our office. They blocked the entrance, barged into the office and arrested him. The place of arrest has been shown as my office. This happened in the middle of the consultation Milord, are we living in a police state?” he asked and insisted upon framing of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

Denying the claim, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan and Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) Arun Anbumani told the court the police were conscious of the law that an accused could not be arrested inside an advocate’s office. They asserted that the former Minister was not arrested inside the lawyer’s office. The SPP said, the police were invited into the lawyer’s office after they were waiting outside for about 90 minutes.

Mr. Anbumani said, the former Minister’s counsel-on-record Richardson Wilson had called the policemen inside the office. “It was a ploy. He called the policemen to come inside the office and has the audacity to come and complain to this court,” the APP added. However, Mr. Richardson denied he called the policemen inside and accused the APP of not instructing the SPP properly.

After hearing both sides, Justice Lakshminarayanan pointed out that district judge L.S. Sathyamurthy did not appear to have accepted the argument of the former Minister having been arrested inside the lawyer’s office while remanding him in judicial custody during the intervening night between Monday and Tuesday. Mr. Wilson replied he would challenge the finding given by the district judge.

When the arguments led to a heated exchange between the prosecution and defense counsel, the SPP said: “This is unfortunate. Let him not distort facts. This is what is happening in this case. Personal attacks are happening. We are also lawyers. This (public prosecutor) is not a permanent position. We don’t have any political affiliations. We are only doing our duty.”

Mr. Sathyan said, he had asked the policemen as to how could they enter a lawyer’s office but the instantaneous answer was that they were invited in to the office. “He (the investigating officer in the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Police attached to CCB) said, I have material to show that I was invited into his office. If it is so required, we will place the material before the court.”

Justice Lakshminarayanan asked Mr. Richardson to produce the CCTV footage from his office along with the audio recording since the footage produced on Thursday had only visuals but no audio. The judge thereafter adjourned the hearing on the FIR quash plea to November 10, 2026 since a similar question of law had to be decided in another case related to former Minister E.V. Velu.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 30 Oct 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

However, State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan denies the allegation and says the police were actually invited into the office but they did not arrest the accused inside the lawyer’s office

Senior counsel P. Wilson on Thursday (October 29, 2026) complained to the Madras High Court that Central Crime Branch (CCB) police personnel “barged” into his office in Chennai on October 26, 2026 to arrest former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi (DMK) in a case booked on charges of allegedly collecting over ₹400 crore towards ‘party fund’ from more than 177 private school managements in the State.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, seized of a plea by the former Minister to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against him, the senior counsel said, the petitioner was at his office on Nelson Manickam Road at about 3 p.m. on Monday to discuss about the further course of legal action to be taken pursuant to the dismissal of his anticipatory bail petition by the High Court.

“We were discussing at our office regarding further course of legal action. About three vans of 40 policemen came to our office. They blocked the entrance, barged into the office and arrested him. The place of arrest has been shown as my office. This happened in the middle of the consultation Milord, are we living in a police state?” he asked and insisted upon framing of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

Denying the claim, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan and Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) Arun Anbumani told the court the police were conscious of the law that an accused could not be arrested inside an advocate’s office. They asserted that the former Minister was not arrested inside the lawyer’s office. The SPP said, the police were invited into the lawyer’s office after they were waiting outside for about 90 minutes.

Mr. Anbumani said, the former Minister’s counsel-on-record Richardson Wilson had called the policemen inside the office. “It was a ploy. He called the policemen to come inside the office and has the audacity to come and complain to this court,” the APP added. However, Mr. Richardson denied he called the policemen inside and accused the APP of not instructing the SPP properly.

After hearing both sides, Justice Lakshminarayanan pointed out that district judge L.S. Sathyamurthy did not appear to have accepted the argument of the former Minister having been arrested inside the lawyer’s office while remanding him in judicial custody during the intervening night between Monday and Tuesday. Mr. Wilson replied he would challenge the finding given by the district judge.

When the arguments led to a heated exchange between the prosecution and defense counsel, the SPP said: “This is unfortunate. Let him not distort facts. This is what is happening in this case. Personal attacks are happening. We are also lawyers. This (public prosecutor) is not a permanent position. We don’t have any political affiliations. We are only doing our duty.”

Mr. Sathyan said, he had asked the policemen as to how could they enter a lawyer’s office but the instantaneous answer was that they were invited in to the office. “He (the investigating officer in the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Police attached to CCB) said, I have material to show that I was invited into his office. If it is so required, we will place the material before the court.”

Justice Lakshminarayanan asked Mr. Richardson to produce the CCTV footage from his office along with the audio recording since the footage produced on Thursday had only visuals but no audio. The judge thereafter adjourned the hearing on the FIR quash plea to November 10, 2026 since a similar question of law had to be decided in another case related to former Minister E.V. Velu.

3. articles.title: Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen sent to 13 days police custody
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indranil Sen served as the tourism and culture minister during the Mamata Banerjee era

Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen was sent to 13 days of police custody on Thursday (October 29). The Trinamool Congress-era minister was arrested on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) in relation to a Durga Puja ticket scam.

“We have got 13 days PC of ex-MIC Indranil Sen till 10th Nov,” a statement from Kunal Agarwal, Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime), said. He was produced at the Bankshall Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) morning.

Police have said that they have found multiple transactions linked to Mr. Sen, which the former minister has not been able to explain. He will be in police custody for further questioning. He had been avoiding the police even after multiple summons.
“The exact amount of cheating and money trail is still being verified. No precise figure can be provided at present. The complaint made is of 34 crore,” police also said.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), Bharatiya Janata Party workers staged a protest outside Mr. Sen’s house in the Singur area. They also dragged a man with a rope tied around his waist and put a picture of Mr. Sen on his face.

Both the Kolkata Police and the Enforcement Directorate are investigating the former minister for allegations of financial irregularities in the sale of Durga Puja tickets under the organisation MassArt. The organisation is headed by his wife and used to conduct exclusive Durga Puja previews in exchange for expensive tickets.
An FIR at the Bow Bazar Police Station has alleged Mr. Sen and the other members of MassArt had used the Durga Puja’s UNESCO intangible cultural heritage tag for personal gains.

After Mr. Sen’s arrest on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and minister Agnimitra Paul both raised allegations that if Mr. Sen has “stolen money, he shared the proceeds with the former CM Mamata Banerjee.”
“Indranil Sen’s arrest is natural, but will the arrests reach the top of these scams?” senior Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader Sujan Chakraborty asked.
However, Mamata-Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said that anyone who has not sold their spine is being put behind bars.

articles.title: Any plan to restrict sale of liquor in hotel bars and clubs located close to educational institutions? Madras High Court asks Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Ramesh poses the question after expressing shock over a 19-year-old college student having consumed liquor at a bar attached to a hotel reportedly run by the college management

The Madras High Court has directed the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise to spell out whether any norms would be put in place for licensing bars inside hotels/clubs located near educational institutions in order to prevent incidents of underage students being offered liquor and ending up in fisticuffs in an inebriated mood.

Justice N. Ramesh issued the direction after expressing shock over a criminal case registered against a 19-year-old college student for having allegedly indulged in a brawl with fellow students when they were consuming liquor at a bar attached to an adjacent hotel reportedly run by the college management.

The judge suo motu impleaded the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise as one of the respondents to an anticipatory bail petition filed by the college student and called for details regarding the licence issued to El Dorado bar at SRM Hotel in Potheri, near Chennai.

He also wanted the Commissioner to explain whether there were any rules, government orders, circulars or any other guidelines governing the grant and renewal of licence in Form F.L.3, and whether any of them prescribe a minimum distance from an educational institution, a students’ hostel or a place of worship.

The Commissioner was further directed to furnish to the court the distance between the bar and the nearest gate/ building/hostel of the educational institution measured along the path a pedestrian would ordinarily take, and whether the premises lies within a municipal area.

The officer was also ordered to state whether the proximity of the educational institution and the number of students studying there was taken into consideration before granting/renewing the FL3 licence to the bar in the hotel and what action would be taken in future.

Justice Ramesh also impleaded the SRM Institute of Science and Technology as another respondent to the petition and directed its Registrar to disclose whether the college management had any connection whatsoever with SRM Hotel and the steps taken by it to prevent students from consuming alcohol.

Taking note that three students who got injured due to a hit with a beer bottle on September 26, 2026 had been treated at SRM Hospital, the judge ordered that the petitioner should not be arrested until further orders provided he cooperates with the investigation and appears for inquiry whenever required.

Justice N. Ramesh poses the question after expressing shock over a 19-year-old college student having consumed liquor at a bar attached to a hotel reportedly run by the college management

The Madras High Court has directed the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise to spell out whether any norms would be put in place for licensing bars inside hotels/clubs located near educational institutions in order to prevent incidents of underage students being offered liquor and ending up in fisticuffs in an inebriated mood.

Justice N. Ramesh issued the direction after expressing shock over a criminal case registered against a 19-year-old college student for having allegedly indulged in a brawl with fellow students when they were consuming liquor at a bar attached to an adjacent hotel reportedly run by the college management.

The judge suo motu impleaded the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise as one of the respondents to an anticipatory bail petition filed by the college student and called for details regarding the licence issued to El Dorado bar at SRM Hotel in Potheri, near Chennai.

He also wanted the Commissioner to explain whether there were any rules, government orders, circulars or any other guidelines governing the grant and renewal of licence in Form F.L.3, and whether any of them prescribe a minimum distance from an educational institution, a students’ hostel or a place of worship.

The Commissioner was further directed to furnish to the court the distance between the bar and the nearest gate/ building/hostel of the educational institution measured along the path a pedestrian would ordinarily take, and whether the premises lies within a municipal area.

The officer was also ordered to state whether the proximity of the educational institution and the number of students studying there was taken into consideration before granting/renewing the FL3 licence to the bar in the hotel and what action would be taken in future.

Justice Ramesh also impleaded the SRM Institute of Science and Technology as another respondent to the petition and directed its Registrar to disclose whether the college management had any connection whatsoever with SRM Hotel and the steps taken by it to prevent students from consuming alcohol.

Taking note that three students who got injured due to a hit with a beer bottle on September 26, 2026 had been treated at SRM Hospital, the judge ordered that the petitioner should not be arrested until further orders provided he cooperates with the investigation and appears for inquiry whenever required.

articles.title: M.P. wildlife officials highlight Chambal region’s gun culture as probe into cheetah shooting goes on
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speaking to The Hindu, an official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers

The wildlife officials in Madhya Pradesh have raised questions about the prevalent gun culture in the Chambal region even as they continue their investigation into the killing of a 19-month-old cheetah cub who was found with five gunshot injuries on October 25. The cub passed away on the morning of October 27 during treatment in Jabalpur.

Speaking to The Hindu , a high-ranking official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers in the region. The probe is yet to make a breakthrough.

“It’s a very complex dynamics there with almost everybody owning a gun so we will have to target this culture too going forward. There is need to review the criteria of issuing a gun license in the region and we hope there is some discussion about this at the government level,” the official said requesting anonymity, while calling for a crackdown on the illegal gun manufacturing in the region.
The conversation on gun culture coming up in the probe was confirmed by State’s Chief Wildlife Warden (CWLW) Sameeta Rajora.
Ms. Rajora said that all possible angles, including poaching, revenge killing or self-defence, were being explored in the probe.

On the evening of October 25, a cheetah monitoring team found the cub, which was wearing a radio collar for tracking, in a still position in compartment no. 748 of the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division on the border of Sheopur and Morena districts, about 50 kilometres from Kuno’s boundaries. During treatment in Jabalpur, five firearm metal pellets were recovered from his body, including one from his lung.

The two districts fall under the Chambal region, which was once infamous for its vast ravines and the dacoits hiding in them. Even though the dacoits are a fear of the past now, rivalries, high crime rates, and the tradition of owning a gun continue to thrive in the region. Morena is often in the news for its illegal arms manufacturing.
Officials from the region say a gun can be found in almost every household there.

The probe is being carried out by a State Government-formed special task force (STF) of forest and police officers, while a high-level team constituted by the Union Government also visited the area on October 28.
Sources in Kuno said that various teams had been mapping the area roamed by the cub for 15-20 days before he was shot for leads.

articles.title: A security deal, but not the end of the Arctic contest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Greenland agreement strengthens American security while raising sovereignty concerns

The agreement signed between the United States, Denmark and Greenland on September 22, 2026, marks an important moment in the changing geopolitics of the Arctic. Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. Greenland came into the news this year because of the Trump administration’s repeated interest in gaining control over the island. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic.

The agreement, signed at the United Nations, expands the American military presence in Greenland while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination. It brings, at least for now, an end to the unusual tensions between Washington and Copenhagen over the future of the strategically important island. The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland.

Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic.

The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland.

articles.title: Labour Ministry sets up National Social Security Boards for unorganised, gig and platform workers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The mandate of the Boards include design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to gig and platform workers and traditional unorganised workers
The Union Labour Ministry on Friday (October 30, 2026), constituted National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers, and Gig & Platform Workers.

Union Minister for Labour and Employment Mansukh Mandaviya will be the chairman of both boards, which will have representatives from Central and State Governments, prominent aggregator companies, employers, civil society organisations, workers’ unions and gig and platform Associations .
The mandate of the Boards would be to design, monitor and recommend targeted welfare schemes to gig and platform workers and traditional unorganised workers.
The Boards will meet at least thrice a year and the Union Government will prescribe the rules of procedure for them.

The functions of the board include recommending suitable schemes for different sections of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers; advising the Union Government on the administration of the Social Security Code; monitoring social welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers; reviewing the record-keeping functions performed at the State level; reviewing the expenditure from the fund and account; and undertaking other functions assigned to it by the Union Government from time to time.

articles.title: Terror financing module: 10 associates of terrorists arrested in J&K

The arrests were made following a focused investigation into suspected financial networks linked to terrorist activities, the officials said.

“During the investigation, suspicious online financial transactions carried out through various payment platforms were analysed, leading to the tracing of money trails across multiple layers. The investigation revealed a wider network of individuals allegedly involved in terror financing and having links with terrorists and their associates lodged in different jails,” they said.
Ten associates of terrorists have been arrested in connection with the case so far, the officials added.

articles.title: CTI urges Congress to postpone November 1 rally, says ₹10,000-12,000 crore trade in Delhi markets at risk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter to Sonia Gandhi, the traders' body said the proposed rally, which is expected to draw 10 lakh people, could affect business worth ₹10,000-12,000 crore in wholesale and retail markets in central and old Delhi during the peak festive season

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to postpone the party's proposed November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali, citing concerns over disruption to business in 20 major markets in the national capital that could affect business worth ₹10,000-12,000 crore.

The traders' body has made two suggestions to Sonia Gandhi — postpone the rally until November 10-11 or later, or shift the venue from Ramlila Maidan to Burari Ground, where it claimed there is parking space for around 15,000 vehicles.

CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said the organisation had earlier written three letters to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, requesting him to reconsider the rally's timing, but had now approached Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi with its appeal.

In a letter to Sonia Gandhi, the traders' body said the proposed rally, which is expected to draw 10 lakh people, could affect business worth ₹10,000-12,000 crore in wholesale and retail markets in central and old Delhi during the peak festive season.
Mr. Goyal said the traders were not opposing the rally but were concerned about the timing, as Dhanteras falls on November 6 and Diwali on November 8.
"November 1 is a crucial day for preparations for Diwali. If 10 lakh people and 15,000-20,000 vehicles enter central Delhi, business in 20 major markets could come to a standstill," he said.
The CTI said there was inadequate parking space at Ramlila Maidan to accommodate the estimated 15,000-20,000 vehicles expected to bring participants of the rally.
It said the vehicles could spill over onto major roads, including JLN Marg, Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg and Netaji Subhash Marg, potentially leading to severe traffic congestion in central and old Delhi.
"The traders are worried about how goods for Dhanteras will reach the markets if central Delhi faces severe traffic congestion on October 31 and November 1," he said.

The traders' body identified markets such as Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Connaught Place, Khari Baoli, Bhagirath Palace, Kashmere Gate, Chawri Bazar, Karol Bagh and Dariba Kalan among those that could be affected.

articles.title: Telangana sends 2,000 staff, material to A.P. for power supply restoration work
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana dispatched nearly 2,000 staff along with emergency materials from its two distribution utilities to assist Andhra Pradesh in restoring power after the Arnab cyclone

The two distribution utilities of Telangana have dispatched emergency material along with nearly 2,000 staff to help restoration of power supply in the Arnab cyclone-hit areas in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, following a request from that State.

Several power staff teams were sent to the cyclone-hit areas from Telangana on Tuesday along with some emergency material required for restoration of power supply. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Energy Minister G. Ravi Kumar spoke to their Telangana counterparts A. Revanth Reddy and M. Bhatti Vikramarka, respectively, over phone on Tuesday and sought help in restoration of power supply.

It was explained that over 16,000 electric poles fell due to the cyclone in Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Eluru, NTR, Guntur, Pravathipuram, Alluri Sitaramaraju, and a few other districts. A.P. has the help of men and material from Telangana for the restoration work.

On getting instructions from Mr. Vikramarka the Chairmen and Managing Directors of TGSPDCL and TGNPDCL Jitesh V. Patil and K. Varun Reddy deputed the team from their Discoms to A.P. along with some material. While SPDCL is sending over 1,300 of its staff, NPDCL is sending nearly 650 staff along with emergency response vehicles, battery-powered tree pruners and other equipment.
Deputy Chief Minister Mr. Vikramarka said the deputation of men and material to A.P. for the power supply restoration work was an indication of brotherhood between the two Telugu States.

articles.title: Glacial lake outburst in Bhutan triggers flood alert in northern West Bengal, Assam
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Following reports of flash floods in the river’s upper reaches, water levels in the Sankosh could rise suddenly in Assam’s Dhubri and West Bengal’s Alipurduar districts, says advisory

A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Bhutan has triggered a high flood alert in parts of northern West Bengal, prompting evacuations in areas along the Sankosh River and its tributaries amid fears of a sudden rise in water levels, officials said on Friday (October 30, 2026).
Residents of riverbank villages in Alipurduar district were seen leaving their homes with their cattle after the administration issued evacuation instructions.

Water Resources Investigation and Development Minister Nisith Pramanik said a glacial outburst had occurred at Lemthang in Bhutan, with water from the lake flowing through the Mo (Mofu) River towards the Sankosh.

“Everyone living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh River and all its connected tributaries has been asked to move to a safe distance immediately to protect their lives,” Mr. Pramanik said in a video message.
He urged residents living near riverbeds in Tufanganj and adjoining areas in Cooch Behar to evacuate immediately in view of the potential flooding.

He said the administration was prepared to deal with any eventuality, with teams of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) kept on alert for rescue and relief operations.

A glacier lake outburst flood (GLOF) which has originated from the Sintaphu lake at Mochu subbasin Gasa has been reported. The NCHM is currently monitoring the water level along the Mochu river at Tashithang. India has been informed. https://t.co/ArS7S73wd2
Darjeeling MP Raju Bista urged people in the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions to remain vigilant and follow official advisories.

Nearly 7.4 million cubic metres of water had surged out of the breached Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan into the Mo River, raising fears of a sudden increase in the water level of the Sankosh, which flows along the West Bengal-Assam border.

“The administration began evacuation measures late Thursday night (October 29) in villages along the Sankosh. Loudspeaker announcements were made in riverbank settlements under the Rampur-I gram panchayat area, asking residents to leave their homes and move to designated shelters,” officials said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu' s party has amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance, as final results showed his bloc had lost its majority in parliament.

The opposition accused Mr. Netanyahu of demonising the Arab population after a historic showing by Arab-led parties in an attempt to delegitimise the election. If the rest of the opposition teams up with Arab parties, a rare and politically risky move, they could potentially form a majority government in parliament, the Knesset.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology, observes testing of weapons
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” says Korean Central News Agency

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for rapidly expanding the country's drone technology and observed tests of various weapons, state media reported Friday (October 30, 2026), as his nation remains embroiled in a standoff with rival South Korea along their heavily fortified border.

Acquiring advanced drones is a top priority for Mr. Kim, who now wants to beef up both conventional and nuclear capabilities. Experts say his troops dispatched to Russia to support its war against Ukraine have likely gained valuable expertise in drone warfare from Russian forces and related battlefield experiences.

The North’s official Korean Central News Agency said that Mr. Kim on Thursday (October 29) visited an exhibition of a variety of attack and other drones that show recent achievements in the field of unmanned aeronautical technology.

In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” KCNA said.

To mark the event, KCNA said that North Korea later conducted test launches of various drones, missiles and weapons from the 600 mm-calibre ultra-precision multiple rocket launchers. KCNA photos showed Mr. Kim watching soaring weapons or him clenching his fist while his teenage daughter was clapping her hands beside him. South Korea's spy agency assesses that the girl, reportedly about 13, is likely Mr. Kim's heir.

South Korea's military earlier said it detected the launches of about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from North Korea's eastern coastal town of Wonsan on Thursday (October 29). They were North Korea's first ballistic weapons firings in 17 days.

Tensions between the two Koreas have been running high since last month's land mine blasts at their border that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul accused North Korea of burying the mines south of the military demarcation line and demanded an apology. But Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked.
Last week, North Korea threatened to resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts and place new weapons systems along the border.

North Korea has pulled out of talks with the U.S. and South Korea after Mr. Kim's high-stakes diplomacy with U.S. President Donald Trump collapsed in 2019. In recent weeks, North Korea has dialled up weapons testing activities in a likely attempt to boost its leverage in potential diplomacy with the U.S. after Trump expressed his eagerness to restore talks with Mr. Kim.

On Saturday (October 24), Mr. Kim made a surprise visit to a Chinese border town via a newly opened bridge and vowed to develop bilateral ties. Mr. Kim has recently taken steps to cement ties with China, North Korea's economic pipeline, after years of prioritising ties with Russia, including by supplying thousands of troops and ammunition, likely in return for economic and military assistance.

articles.title: Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: investments have raised a nagging question among some doubters on Wall Street: is Nvidia helping to inflate an AI bubble?

Nvidia's $3 billion investment in Meta's share sale, announced Tuesday, is the latest addition to a portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees that has made the chip giant what some analysts describe as the central bank of the artificial intelligence boom.
The galaxy of deals has helped keep demand running high for Nvidia's processors, which power vast data centres around the world and are the central ingredient of the AI revolution.
That demand has made Nvidia the world's most valuable company by market capitalisation and turned chief executive Jensen Huang into AI's kingmaker.
But the investments have raised a nagging question among some doubters on Wall Street: is Nvidia helping to inflate an AI bubble?
Nvidia has taken stakes in leading AI developers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX.
It has also invested in "neocloud" companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius, which rent out computing power built on Nvidia chips.

Its bets extend well beyond the United States. In Europe, Nvidia has backed French AI developer Mistral and British self-driving startup Wayve. In Asia, it has teamed up with South Korea's SK Group to build data centers.
Beyond equity, the company has offered financial backstops, acting as a customer of last resort.
In CoreWeave's case, Nvidia committed to buy up to $6.3 billion of unused computing capacity if no other customer takes it.
Nvidia also has around $36 billion in cloud backstops and a guarantee of up to $105 billion linked to an OpenAI data centre, according to US media.

articles.title: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound
In 1904, two scientists, Henry Wheeler and Treat Johnson, synthesised a variant of cytosine, one of the building blocks of DNA, in the laboratory.

The variant they synthesised contained a chemical tag called a methyl group (-CH 3 ) attached to cytosine, so they called it 5-methylcytosine. Their motivation for doing so was based on the observation that two other building blocks of DNA and its chemical cousin RNA, called thymine and uracil, differed only by the presence of a methyl group.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Tech firms were again on the back foot Friday after another round of disappointing earnings from Wall Street titans fanned already deep concerns about the AI investment boom.

AI-linked tech firms suffered steep losses after Amazon's quarterly report fell short of analyst expectations on profit and revenue, and Intel's expected income missed estimates owing to weak demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems.
The announcements came a day after Google parent Alphabet reported soft growth in revenue from advertising and its search business , while saying it would ramp up capital expenditure.

Alphabet plunged more than 12 percent, while Amazon tanked more than seven percent in after-hours trade, having lost more than four percent before the close, while Intel cratered 23 percent. The Nasdaq finished down more than one percent.

Japanese semiconductor firm Kioxia shed more than nine percent, as did Advantest, while SoftBank skidded around seven percent.

"The concern isn't that AI demand has already slowed. It's that higher funding costs and credit risk could eventually force hyperscalers to slow their build-out."
The selloff hit most broader markets in the region, with Seoul diving more than five percent, Tokyo shedding more than two percent and Taipei more than three percent.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.summary: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab
articles.keyPoints:
• Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab
• Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.
• Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court flags irony: Law meant to curb red tapism bogged down it
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, noting that none of the present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law

Noticing delays from 466 days to 1,099 days in filling appeals against judgments, the High Court of Karnataka has said that the State government enacted the Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, “to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of this law.”

A Division Bench comprising Justice M. Nagaprasanna and Justice Hema Kulkarni made these observations on the four appeals filed by the State government challenging verdicts of a single judge related to service of certain employees in the Karnataka State Law University.

Apart from various judgments of the apex court on delay in filling appeals by the State authorities, the State-enacted Act of 2023 clearly prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, while pointing out that that none of present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law on conduct of litigation.

“The time limits prescribed for movement of files, securing opinions, and taking decisions appear to have been thrown to the winds. The State, which enacted the law to bring order and accountability into governmental litigation, has itself failed to demonstrate fidelity to its mandate. The irony is unmistakable: the State enacted a law to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of the law, Bench observed.

The Bench noted that the explanations offered for the delays — files moving from table to table, correspondence passing from officer to officer, legal opinions being sought and documents collected — merely chronicled administrative activity without establishing sufficient cause to condone the delay in filling of the appeal.

“The State is expected to be a model litigant, not a privileged procrastinator. Its obligation is to uphold the rule of law, not to seek exceptions from its operation,” the Bench said while observing that “a law enacted by the State cannot remain a mere ornament in the statute book, commanding obedience from everyone except its own author.

Stating that applications filed by the State government explaining reason for the enormous delay “disclose no exceptional circumstance, no compelling impediment and no credible explanation that could constitute sufficient cause for the extraordinary delays,” the Bench said, while observing that “what is presented as an explanation is, in substance, an assortment of administrative excuses; what is sought as judicial indulgence would, if granted, amount to judicial endorsement of bureaucratic apathy.”
Terming one of the applications a “verbatim reproduction” of another, the Bench said a “copy-and-paste explanation cannot become a passport to condonation of delay”.

articles.title: Unmarried rural youth in Maharashtra plan Statewide stir for government help in getting brides
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Core demands of the youth planning to protest include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce

It is not the inflation, unemployment, deletion of names from the voters’ list or corruption that is simmering in rural Maharashtra youth who are gearing up for an agitation. Unlike other Gen Z across India, these youth have an unusual demand – get us brides to marry.

“We are planning not only a Statewide but a nationwide network of boys who are not getting brides to marry and plan a massive agitation,” Kisan Nanaware, a 28-year-old youth from Solapur, told The Hindu .

Mr. Nanaware came into the limelight after he held a dharna demanding bride at the District Collector’s office in September. He fears he may suffer the same fate as thousands of men in rural Solapur in western Maharashtra, pointing out that the issue stretches far beyond men in their early 30s, with some in their 40s and 50s having given up hope of finding a partner.

Youth such as Mr. Nanaware argue that the State must issue an official resolution detailing steps to assist those who are unmarried. Their core demands include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce. He warns that if authorities fail to act, the movement could take an aggressive turn.
The politicians who have been facing various kinds of agitations are now facing heat of the unmarried youth.

What was supposed to be a standard campaign stop for the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections in Ashti, Beed district (Marathwada region), took a dramatic turn when an agitated young man seized the microphone from local organisers and voiced an issue cutting across rural Maharashtra for which he wanted an immediate answer from the leaders. “Keep aside all other problems and look at our condition,” he demanded, speaking to a crowd of ruling alliance leaders gathered for the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituency elections held on October 23. “Many of us, including me, have crossed 30 or 32 and still we are not getting brides. Solve this problem first!”

Leaders of the BJP-led ruling coalition were not entirely surprised by the outburst. Behind the scenes, politicians have been monitoring simmering anger among rural men who find themselves systematically rejected by prospective brides and their families due to falling farm incomes, lack of steady employment, and a skewed gender ratio.

Maharashtra recorded a sex ratio of 899 girls per 1,000 boys during the 2022-24 period, marginally improving from 896 girls in 2012-14 but well below the national average of 918 girls, according to the latest Sample Registration System Statistical Report.

From Ministers to leaders across party lines, veteran leader Sharad Pawar to local gram panchayat sarpanches, young boys are now raising one simple question, “What about our marriage?” No one has answer to this.

“If not leaders, who is going to answer? At least they must solve one problem and this is the pressing one,” said 32-year-old Avinash Shende from Yavatmal in Vidarbha region. Along with farming, he is working on a contract with a private cleaning agency and has not completed his graduation. He added that like him other youth in the region are now galvanising support to take up this issue at the State level. He says the movement would start from gram sabhas in villages.

Core demands of the youth planning to protest include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce

It is not the inflation, unemployment, deletion of names from the voters’ list or corruption that is simmering in rural Maharashtra youth who are gearing up for an agitation. Unlike other Gen Z across India, these youth have an unusual demand – get us brides to marry.

“We are planning not only a Statewide but a nationwide network of boys who are not getting brides to marry and plan a massive agitation,” Kisan Nanaware, a 28-year-old youth from Solapur, told The Hindu .

Mr. Nanaware came into the limelight after he held a dharna demanding bride at the District Collector’s office in September. He fears he may suffer the same fate as thousands of men in rural Solapur in western Maharashtra, pointing out that the issue stretches far beyond men in their early 30s, with some in their 40s and 50s having given up hope of finding a partner.

Youth such as Mr. Nanaware argue that the State must issue an official resolution detailing steps to assist those who are unmarried. Their core demands include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce. He warns that if authorities fail to act, the movement could take an aggressive turn.

The politicians who have been facing various kinds of agitations are now facing heat of the unmarried youth.

What was supposed to be a standard campaign stop for the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections in Ashti, Beed district (Marathwada region), took a dramatic turn when an agitated young man seized the microphone from local organisers and voiced an issue cutting across rural Maharashtra for which he wanted an immediate answer from the leaders. “Keep aside all other problems and look at our condition,” he demanded, speaking to a crowd of ruling alliance leaders gathered for the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituency elections held on October 23. “Many of us, including me, have crossed 30 or 32 and still we are not getting brides. Solve this problem first!”

Leaders of the BJP-led ruling coalition were not entirely surprised by the outburst. Behind the scenes, politicians have been monitoring simmering anger among rural men who find themselves systematically rejected by prospective brides and their families due to falling farm incomes, lack of steady employment, and a skewed gender ratio.

Maharashtra recorded a sex ratio of 899 girls per 1,000 boys during the 2022-24 period, marginally improving from 896 girls in 2012-14 but well below the national average of 918 girls, according to the latest Sample Registration System Statistical Report.

From Ministers to leaders across party lines, veteran leader Sharad Pawar to local gram panchayat sarpanches, young boys are now raising one simple question, “What about our marriage?” No one has answer to this.

“If not leaders, who is going to answer? At least they must solve one problem and this is the pressing one,” said 32-year-old Avinash Shende from Yavatmal in Vidarbha region. Along with farming, he is working on a contract with a private cleaning agency and has not completed his graduation. He added that like him other youth in the region are now galvanising support to take up this issue at the State level. He says the movement would start from gram sabhas in villages.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab to weaken into depression on October 29, says IMD | LIVE updates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At least 17 districts of southern Odisha affected by heavy rainfall due to cyclonic storm Arnab; Andhra Pradesh records five deaths as CM Naidu announces relief measures

A day after various parts of Telangana received rain under the impact of cyclonic storm Arnab, isolated places in 12 districts are likely to receive thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds on Thursday (October 29). The very severe cyclonic storm crossed Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning, before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm.

The 12 districts where thunderstorms have been forecast are Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda districts, as per the India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre’s latest weather bulletin.

With severe cyclonic storm Arnab making landfall along the Andhra coast, rainfall activity is likely to ease considerably across Keralam. With the rains subsiding, daytime temperatures are expected to rise noticeably across the State. The dry spell is likely to persist until another weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal, with the mercury expected to climb during the intervening period.

Cyclone Arnab brought back grim memories of ‘Cyclone Hudhud’, which battered the city 12 years ago. Although ‘Arnab’ was less severe and did not make landfall in the city, the strong winds through the night, extensive damage to the city’s green cover, uprooted electric poles, prolonged power outages and disrupted mobile network connectivity reminded residents of the destruction caused by Hudhud in October 2014.

Residents took to social media to compare their experiences of the two cyclones. People recalled sleepless nights, prolonged power cuts and following the district administration’s instructions to remain indoors unless faced with an emergency.
Cyclone Arnab triggers memories of Hudhud’s 2014 destruction in Vizag, with power outages, uprooted trees, and renewed warnings.

Telangana Deputy Chief Minister and Energy Minister Bhatti Vikramarka spoke to Andhra Pradesh Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar over the phone on Wednesday to enquire about the impact of Cyclone Arnab.

Mr. Vikramarka assured Andhra Pradesh of the Telangana government’s full support in dealing with the situation. He said Telangana was ready to provide personnel and essential materials for restoring the damaged power supply infrastructure, if required.

Mr. Ravi Kumar briefed Mr. Vikramarka on the relief and restoration operations being carried out under the guidance of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and thanked the Telangana government for its support.

Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has postponed polling for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections from November 3 to November 5 because the counting of votes for the urban local body (ULB) elections is to be done on November 3 under the revised schedule.

Around 64.5 lakh electors are potentially missing from the final electoral rolls of Karnataka released after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), based on the Elector-to-Population (E-to-P) ratio of 66.11 released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO).

The State’s E-to-P ratio quoted in the CEO’s statements was calculated as the ratio between the total number of electors on the rolls and the estimated population in 2026 in all age groups, including those below 18 years of age and not eligible to vote.
